frase_gancho.texto: A clay portrait made to accompany a nobleman on his last journey.

puente_narrativo.texto: Now a figurine from the island of Jaina: it was not a toy, but the portrait of a great lord.

guion_corto.texto: They were not toys. The figurines of the island of Jaina were portraits of real people, made to accompany the dead. This one shows a Halach Uinic, a great lord, seated on a throne with a serene and dignified bearing. He wears a headdress with the head of a serpent, a beaded breastplate, and a trimmed beard. It stands 22 centimeters tall. It is made of clay, shaped by hand and in a mold, and dates to the Late Classic. Jaina, in Campeche, was a sanctuary on an island and the necropolis of the Maya elite. These figurines are believed to have been placed in burials to accompany the deceased on their journey to the underworld.

guion_largo.texto:
Jaina means the house on the water. It is a small island, 32 kilometers northeast of the port of Campeche. And it was a great necropolis.

There, the Maya elite buried their dead together with clay figurines. They were not everyday ornaments. They were individualized portraits, placed in tombs to accompany the deceased on their journey to the underworld.

This figurine shows a Halach Uinic. The term translates as true man and was applied to a great lord, a dignitary. He is seated on a throne, with a serene and dignified bearing. He wears a headdress with the head of a serpent, a beaded breastplate, and a trimmed beard. It stands 22 centimeters tall.

It is made of clay, a fine ceramic shaped by hand and in a mold. The pieces from Jaina are hollow, and many work as whistles or rattles. They were decorated with slips and mineral pigments, such as Maya blue, cinnabar red, and white.

It belongs to the Late Classic, between the years 600 and 900 AD.

Look at it as you would at a person. It has posture, rank, and character. And someone made it so that he would not be alone in the tomb.

texto: Look for the headdress with the head of a serpent.
Notice the beaded breastplate and the trimmed beard.
Look at his posture: seated on a throne, with a serene bearing.

texto.Dimensions: 22 cm high x 9.5 cm wide x 7.0 cm deep

texto.pregunta: Myth: The Jaina figurines were toys.
texto.respuesta: Reality: They were individualized portraits, placed in burials to accompany the deceased on their journey to the underworld.
